wv_cotton_hill.blurb: Cotton Hill is a group of crags in the New River Gorge of West Virginia, with Cotton Top among the farthest-downstream crags of the gorge. Cotton Top sits about ten minutes by car from Fayetteville. Sport routes make up the largest share of the climbing, with a good number of boulder problems and some trad alongside. Roped grades run from 5.7 to 5.12 and are centered on 5.10, while the boulders cover a wide spread from easy to very hard. Cotton Top holds the most climbs, with sport routes and big boulders scattered over a hillside, and those boulders are climbed from early fall through early spring. Cotton Club is a continuous cliff of sport and trad moderates, though part of its rock is broken and ledgy. Land of the Lost adds a smaller set of sport climbs.

bc_ladybird_creek.blurb: Ladybird Creek is a bouldering area in the Slocan Valley of the West Kootenay, off Pass Creek Road. Every climb here is a boulder problem, from V0 up to V9, with most falling between V1 and V5 and a handful of hard ones above that. The terrain is varied: technical faces, cracks, roofs, highballs and caves, spread over a large talus slide above the road plus a big boulder beside the creek. The farthest walk is around 15 minutes. The rock is a blend of granite and gneiss, and the area is usually climbed from about April to late October, with fall a highlight when the larches turn yellow. Hemlock/Slide and High Society hold the most climbs.

ca_conejo_boulders.blurb: Conejo Boulders is a bouldering area in the rolling hills of Newbury Park on Conejo Mountain, on California's Central Coast. All of the climbing is bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V4 and a few much harder ones. The rock is breccia, and it breaks often, so holds and topouts deserve a check before trusting them. Landings are generally good. On the mountain, spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons and summer runs hot, and the rock needs a day or two to dry after steady rain. The climbing is spread across several sectors, with Irish Boulders, Hangout Area and Fraggle Rock holding the most problems.

co_buckskin_crags.blurb: Buckskin Crags is a climbing area at Canon City, Colorado, at around 6,300 feet. It mixes styles: sport routes lead, with a solid bouldering component and a smaller amount of trad and top rope. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.11, mostly between 5.8 and 5.10, and the boulder problems stay mainly between V0 and V3. Sun exposure shapes when each cliff is comfortable: north-facing walls suit summer heat, and south-facing ones are warm in winter. At Buddha Wall, the south face is sunny most of the day and the north face is mostly shaded, with fall through spring recommended there. The Sweet Spot holds the most climbs, followed by Buddha Wall and the Slick Rock Gardens boulders.

bc_rockies_2.blurb: The British Columbia Rockies bring together sub-regions including Golden, Yoho, Spillimacheen, the Columbia Icefields, Mount Robson and Mount Assiniboine. Ice makes up the largest share of the climbs, from WI2 to WI6 and mostly WI4 and WI5, and there are commonly climbed ice routes near Field. The rest is mostly sport with some trad, from 5.6 to 5.12 and centered on 5.10. Spillimacheen, south of Golden, is a low-altitude limestone sport crag. The rock of the Rockies is mostly sedimentary. Golden holds the most climbs, followed by Yoho and Spillimacheen.
